correctness.rationale: All geometric points of the power-sum fiber are contained in six affine-F5 root lines by Newton identities and the characteristic-five polynomial U^5+e4 U-e5. A Vandermonde Jacobian and the Cohen--Macaulay complete-intersection criterion prove reducedness. The six transverse branch directions have (2,3) complete-intersection Hilbert ranks 1,3,5,6 from degree zero onward, so normalization delta is 9 and seminormalization defect 4. The conductor contains t^3 on all branches. After quotienting scalar branch constants, the polynomial log 1+v to v-v^2/2 modulo t^3 identifies the connected Picard units group with the four-dimensional additive vector group over F5, not just on rational points. The relative complete intersection is flat, with arithmetic genus 4. The executable exact F5 checker reproduces all six directions, evaluation ranks, group action orbit index, and sample point counts; the algebraic proof establishes the infinite assertions.

value.rationale: This is a canonical highly symmetric genus-four curve with a natural prime-five exceptional fiber, not an arbitrary numerically selected configuration. Its split six-line structure, exact delta-nine singularity, four-dimensional seminormal defect, and additive connected Picard group explain a wild, nonsemistable degeneration beyond mere point counting. The exotic six-component S5 permutation geometry and actual group-scheme classification are potentially useful for comparisons of singular models and generalized Jacobians. No conclusion about stable/Neron reduction is claimed.
